messages.text: Hamilton apologises to Ferrari for overriding strategy call

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton apologised to his Ferrari team for his costly decision to override their strategy call during the Singapore Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton apologises to Ferrari for costly decision to override strategy call during Singapore GP | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lewis Hamilton apologises to Ferrari for costly decision to override strategy call during Singapore GP Lewis Hamilton dropped from third to sixth in the Singapore Grand Prix after choosing not to pit under a Virtual Safety Car; Hamilton was called into the pits by his Ferrari team but opted to stay out; the seven-time world champion required medical checks as he felt unwell after the race Sunday 11 October 2026 19:33, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton apologised to his Ferrari team for his strategy call, which cost them points at the Singapore Grand Prix Lewis Hamilton apologised to his Ferrari team for his costly decision to override their strategy call during the Singapore Grand Prix. Hamilton was running in third behind his team-mate Charles Leclerc on the 39th of 62 laps when a Virtual Safety Car appeared to give him the perfect opportunity to change tyres after he had been the first driver to stop earlier in the race. Ferrari told Hamilton to follow Leclerc into the pits, but he ignored the call and stayed out, which resulted in him finishing the race sixth as he was overtaken by Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri in the closing stages. metadata.summary: Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix for the first time in his Formula 1 career with a dominant victory, while Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton endured a messy race strategically to tumble off the podium late on.
